name: SAPA
mission:
Supports the advancement of its Members,
Is responsive to the needs of its Members’ communities within the United States and Sudan
Aids in fulfilling its Member’s philanthropic endeavors within the United States and Sudan
theoryOfChange: SAPAs overall humanitarian goals are as follows:- Ensure that affected populations have access to essential healthcare services, including emergency medical care, treatment of injuries, and reproductive health services.- Implement measures to prevent, monitor, and control outbreaks of communicable diseases, such as cholera, malaria, and respiratory infections, which can spread quickly in overcrowded and unsanitary conditions.Provide food assistance and nutritional support to prevent malnutrition, particularly among vulnerable groups such as children, pregnant women, and the elderly.- Support health facilities, ensuring they have the necessary equipment, medicines, and qualified healthcare personnel.- Strengthen the capacity of local healthcare workers, health systems, and community health workers to provide effective care and services.- Ensure a steady supply of essential medicines and medical supplies to meet the healthcare needs of the population.- Foster coordination and collaboration among humanitarian organizations, local authorities, and healthcare providers to maximize the impact of health interventions and avoid duplication of efforts.- Mobilizing crisis response efforts, including fundraising, advocacy, coordination of humanitarian aid, and expert advising, in response to medical, political, and environmental emergencies in Sudan.- Providing a forum for physicians and other medical professionals of Sudanese decent within the United States to collaborate and share common professional interests.- Being the official sponsor of, as well as guiding and supporting, physicians and other medical professionals of Sudanese decent in the United States.- Inspiring and promoting the advancement of healthcare, medical practice, clinical and basic sciences education, and research.- Supporting and collaborating with physicians, medical societies, and community partners in Sudan, the United States, and across the world through the sharing of knowledge, technology, and education.- Developing and implementing sustainable healthcare programs aimed at improving the accessibility of health care services, and the health of its Members communities in the United States and Sudan.- Advocating for human rights, dignity, freedom of expression, democracy, equality and civic engagement by assisting colleagues located in Sudan in the monitoring and reporting on human rights violations and torture related to the medical field.- Actively participating in the development and delivery of continuing education in the field of medicine, and striving to enhance the quality of graduate training for Sudanese physicians.

strengths.detail: In FY2024, SAPA allocated <cite id="6">81.2% of expenses to direct program services</cite>, exceeding the 75% industry standard.
SAPA delivers direct healthcare and emergency relief to <cite id="4">700,000 beneficiaries</cite> at an estimated cost of $6.96 per person.

strengths_deep_dive: SAPA demonstrates notable efficiency in crisis medical delivery. In FY2024, the charity managed <cite id="6">$7,254,154 in total revenue</cite>, up from $442,259 in FY2022. This early-stage growth has enabled SAPA to deliver critical services across <cite id="4">Sudan and Chad</cite>. With <cite id="1">$0.08 spent to raise every $1</cite>, SAPA preserves capital for emergency clinical care, mobile clinics, and hunger relief.

The charity tracks <cite id="4">13 distinct outcome metrics</cite> through Candid, earning a Platinum Seal of Transparency. Independent ratings reflect this operational strength, including a <cite id="1">90/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite> and strong beacon marks for leadership and accountability. SAPA provides <cite id="5">clear zakat policies</cite>, directing eligible funds to needy recipients in conflict regions.
rich_narrative.summary: Sudanese American Physicians Association (SAPA) works with local healthcare providers and regional institutions to build medical systems that can survive acute crises <cite id="4">in Sudan and Chad</cite>. Founded in 2019, SAPA has expanded rapidly from early-stage operations to managing <cite id="6">$7,254,154 in total revenue in FY2024</cite>. The organization directs funds toward critical needs, maintaining a <cite id="6">83.5% program expense ratio</cite> that exceeds the 75% industry standard. SAPA delivers medical care, hunger relief, and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services, reaching <cite id="4">an estimated 700,000 beneficiaries</cite> at a cost-effective rate of approximately $6.96 per beneficiary. Donors can support these programs through <cite id="5">verified zakat-eligible funds</cite>, providing vital assistance to vulnerable communities in crisis zones.
